samples.summary: Cross-provider merge gate (`emailVerifiedAt` + `EmailProviderConflictError`) is unrequested scope that lands in the issue's declared Non-Goals and costs existing users the stated outcome on first try
samples.evidence: The originating task (docs/tasks/active/20260915-google-oauth-login-todo.md) decides: "Same email, two providers → one user … The safety condition is that the email be verified — a Google profile whose `email_verified` is false is refused at `GoogleStrategy.validate()`". Its Approach list contains no schema change, and its "Out of scope" section names "Account linking UI, unlinking … showing which provider an existing account was created with". This diff adds a `User.emailVerifiedAt` column + migration and makes `findOrCreateUser` throw `EmailProviderConflictError` whenever an existing row's `emailVerifiedAt` is null and the provider differs. Consequence: for EVERY user row that exists today (all null after the migration), the very first Google sign-in — the flow the issue exists to deliver — is refused with `?error=email_conflict` and the person is told to go sign in with GitHub once first. That is a linking ritual (the out-of-scope item) baked into the data model rather than the one-user-per-email behaviour the issue decided on.

samples.summary: Workspace slug derivation + uniquification is reimplemented in UserService instead of reusing WorkspaceService.generateUniqueSlug, and the two now give different answers
samples.evidence: `workspaceSlugBase`/`freeSlug`/`isSlugConflict` in user.service.ts duplicate `WorkspaceService.generateSlug`/`generateUniqueSlug` (packages/backend/src/workspace/workspace.service.ts:267-287), down to the identical `|| 'workspace'` neutral-base comment. They already disagree: WorkspaceService appends a 4-char base36 suffix with no retry, UserService a 6-hex suffix with 5 retries inside a transaction. Two implementations of "give me a free workspace slug" in a repo whose stated discipline is reuse; a future fix (e.g. a stricter slug charset or a longer suffix) will land in only one.

samples.summary: GitHub login behaviour change (allRawEmails + refuse accounts with no verified address) is outside the issue's approach list and can lock existing GitHub users out
samples.evidence: The task's Approach enumerates the Google-side work only; the verified-email condition is stated for `GoogleStrategy.validate()`. This diff also rewrites `GitHubStrategy.validate` to refuse any account with no verified address (`error: 'unverified_email'`), which changes the only login path every existing deployment has: a user whose GitHub addresses are all unverified can no longer reach their existing account. It is defensible (it is the weaker side of the email merge, and docs/design/backend.md's risk entry records it), but it is a behaviour change to an existing flow that the spec did not ask for and that has user-visible cost.

samples.summary: docs/design/cli.md is not updated for the new `?error=<code>&state=<nonce>` loopback callback shape, and now contradicts itself on "a refusal never ends the wait"
samples.evidence: cli.md documents the loopback contract as step 6 `…/callback?code=<code>&state=<nonce>` (line 198-199) and repeatedly rests its threat model on "A forged hit is answered 403 and does *not* end the wait" / "Because a refusal never ends the wait…" (lines 253-254, 272-279). This change adds a second legitimate callback shape (`?error=`) that DOES end the wait by rejecting with `EXIT_USER_ERROR`, plus `loginRefusalMessage` and a new refusal HTML page in packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts. The CLI design doc — the canonical doc for this protocol — records neither, so the documented invariant now reads as false. (backend.md and frontend.md were updated; cli.md was missed.)

samples.summary: Operator self-hosting guide never says how to enable Google sign-in, while already referencing GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL
samples.evidence: `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` / `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` appear nowhere in packages/documentation (grep over the whole package returns only Analytics/GCS hits), yet self-hosting.md:453-457 already explains that `GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL` participates in the cookie-Secure decision. So the operator-facing deployment guide mentions a variable it never defines and gives no way to discover or turn on the feature this PR ships; only packages/backend/README.md and docs/design/backend.md carry the env table.
searchedFor: grep -r GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID (repo-wide, 9 files, none under packages/documentation)

verdict.reason: Verified independently against the tree. The task doc's Approach list (docs/tasks/active/20260915-google-oauth-login-todo.md:33-57) contains no schema change, and its Decision 1 (lines 14-21) names the strategy-level `email_verified` check as the safety condition for the "same email, two providers -> one user" outcome. The diff nonetheless adds `User.emailVerifiedAt` (prisma/schema.prisma:12) via a migration that explicitly leaves the column NULL for every existing row ("Deliberately NULL for every existing row", migration.sql:1-6), and `findOrCreateUser` throws `EmailProviderConflictError` whenever an existing row's `emailVerifiedAt` is null and the provider differs (user.service.ts:134-138). That refusal is fully reachable end to end: auth.controller.ts:271-276 maps it to `{error:'email_conflict'}`, auth.controller.ts:338-341 redirects the Google callback to `?error=email_conflict`, and login-form.tsx:47-50 tells the person to sign in with the other provider once first. The repo's own test (user.service.spec.ts:180-194) encodes exactly this for a null row. Consequence: for every account existing at deploy time, the first Google sign-in -- the flow the issue exists to deliver -- is refused and a manual sign-in-with-the-other-provider step is imposed, which is the linking ritual adjacent to the doc's Out-of-scope list (todo.md:70-73). No refutation ground holds: the code is present as described, nothing backfills or guards the null population (the migration deliberately declines to), and scope creep / spec conformance is this lens's lane. The backend.md design-doc update (935-947) satisfies doc discipline but does not cure the spec divergence or the user-facing cost.
